messages:
jamie: heads-up - we're seeing a perf regression on qwen-13b serving in dedicated. lots of requests are hitting the fallback matmul kernel during generation when head_dim=77. latency up ~2.8x on p4d canaries :thinking_face:

anita: do you have a repro/config? which kernel chooser is deciding fallback? SDPA/FlashAttention or Triton path?

jamie: reproducer is easy: model variant qwen-13b-77hd, batch=4, seq=1024, kv-cache enabled. runtime logs show `kernel_picker: flashattn incompatible (head_dim 77)` then `fallback: triton_matmul` and finally `fallback: cpu_kv_mul` in rare cases. perf-bot attached a cpu/gpu flame: 
```
Top hotspots (gpu):
  58.4% fallback_triton_matmul
  23.1% kv_cache_copy
   9.5% flash_attn_kernel_selector
   5.0% postprocess_cpu
```

leo: wow head_dim 77. That's not multiple of 8/16 so FlashAttention/SDPA rejects it. Is our selector too conservative? We used an alignment check that rejects any non-multiple-of-8 for safety.

sara: check masking too — we've seen mask pack/unpack assume 128 alignment and produce out-of-bounds when head dim odd. that might be why selector errs on the safe side. any mask errors in logs?

jamie: there are intermittent warnings: `mask_write overrun detected` but no hard crash. suspect logic forces fallback to avoid corruption. i ran microbench: for head_dim=80 we get flashattn working and latency 90ms; for 77 it's 260ms.

anita: can we add a compatibility shim that pads head_dim to next multiple (e.g., 80) at kernel launch time? cheap in kernel but changes kv indexing. risk for RoPE scaling offsets though.

jamie: exactly, RoPE scaling is sensitive. when we pad physical head dim we must adjust rotary_sin/cos offsets and KV layout so the served semantics are identical. naive padding breaks fine-grained RoPE freq indexing -> token drift in long-context tests. saw small perplexity regressions in evals.

leo: idea: implement per-layer kernel wrapper that uses padded storage for compute but exposes logical head_dim 77. steps: allocate aligned buffer, copy/pack KV with stride that respects padding, run flashattn on padded buffers, then unpack. cost = extra mem copy + small CPU/GPU bandwidth. Should be far cheaper than fallback matmul.

perf-bot: perf estimate for shim (on p4d): extra memcpy adds ~12-15% wall time vs native flashattn. fallback triton path is ~220% slower in our tests.

anita: ok good. also need unit tests for RoPE invariants: run rotary embeddings with and without shim across 1k-step recurrence, check L2 error < 1e-6. add a canary eval set (long-context tasks).

jamie: i'll prototype shim. quick patch plan: kernel_picker -> if unsupported head_dim && head_dim % 8 != 0 then try pad_shim; only if shim fails fall back to triton. also add a runtime flag `runtime.allow_head_padding=true` gated by dedicated/private tiers for now.

sara: also audit SDPA code paths: some masking edgecases when seq_len < head_dim and kv cache reuse happened. add regression test that replays cached-kv across different seq_lens. saw a case where mask bits leaked between batches.

leo: repo note: created a small reproducer script in infra/testdata/qwen_headdim_repro.py and pushed to my branch. includes perf logs and nvprof snapshots. PR incoming.

jamie: can someone triage deploy canary? deploy-bot: canary(qwen-13b-77hd) reported 15% error rate and 2.8x p95 latency.

deploy-bot: canary(qwen-13b-77hd) status -> failing. rolling back to previous was triggered at 1773456830.

anita: keep rollback. jamie, prioritize shim + RoPE unit tests. add a small batching heuristic tweak: if padded_shim is used, prefer smaller batch sizes to reduce additional memcpy pressure. we can later tune autoscaler.

jamie: ack. i'll open PR with shim + tests + runtime flag. will include perf numbers, evla diffs, and a script to toggle padding. ETA EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

leo: ping me for kernel review. i want to explore a Triton kernel variant that handles arbitrary head_dims by using dynamic tile sizes — might be more future-proof.

sara: and i'll own masking regression tests + add an e2e eval that runs after any kernel selector change.

jamie: thanks all. saving logs here: https://internal.redwood/p/perf/qwen_headdim_77/ and linking PR once ready.

perf-bot: note: add perf baseline for qwen-13b head_dims [64,77,80,96,128] in the dashboard to track improvements.
